thread:
pagerduty-bot: PAGERDUTY ALERT — geo-dns-resolver-errors triggered for service: inference-api (severity: P2). Multiple clients in eu-west-1 seeing 502/timeout. Incident created. (rule: geo-dns-error-rate > 5% over 2m)

Ava (oncall): saw the alert, pulling it up now. any initial impact numbers?

Jules (netops): seeing inconsistent DNS answers from our geo DNS layer — Route53 returning older A records for many eu-edge hostnames, while Cloudflare returns the expected set. Some resolvers are mixing responses leading to upstream TLS host mismatch and 502s.

Maya (eng-sre): confirmed increased 5xxs in EU. Error spike ~ 14% for synthetic checks hitting eu-edge, started ~1765556600. Affected routes: /v1/generate and /v1/chat (eu region).

Theo (support): Customer report from AcmeCorp: intermittent 502s since ~08:10 UTC, they've degraded end-user experience. Ticket created.

Ava (oncall): tagging netops, provable strategy: 1) reduce TTLs for geo DNS to 30s, 2) force authoritative flush on Cloudflare, 3) shift Route53 weights to fallback pool for eu. Who can run the Route53 change? @Jules

Jules (netops): taking it. Will run a weighted failover to eu-fallback pool and lower TTLs. Pasting commands I plan to run:
```bash
# set Route53 weighted record -> fallback (pseudo)
aws route53 change-resource-record-sets --hosted-zone-id Z123ABC --change-batch '{"Changes":[{"Action":"UPSERT","ResourceRecordSet":{"Name":"edge.example.com","Type":"A","SetIdentifier":"eu-fallback","Weight":100,"TTL":30,"ResourceRecords":[{"Value":"198.51.100.12"}]}}]}'

# Cloudflare purge by cache-tag
curl -X POST "https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/zones/$ZONE/purge_cache" -H "X-Auth-Email: ops@redwood.ai" -H "X-Auth-Key: $KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" --data '{"purge_everything":true}'
```

Maya (eng-sre): I'll watch synthetic checks and traces. Also recommend adding a temporary healthcheck override so Route53 picks the fallback quicker.

infra-bot: Deploy job update: run_id=deploy-3921 queued -> in_progress on netops-runner-3.

Ava (oncall): Jules, once you flip weights, can you post dig outputs (before/after) for a couple EU resolvers? Want to confirm propagation.

Jules (netops): Will do. Running change now.

Jules (netops): DIG before: (from 193.0.113.5 resolver)
```
; <<>> DiG 9.11.3 <<>> edge.example.com @193.0.113.5
;; ANSWER SECTION:
edge.example.com. 300 IN A 203.0.113.21
```

Jules (netops): DIG after (30s):
```
; <<>> DiG 9.11.3 <<>> edge.example.com @193.0.113.5
;; ANSWER SECTION:
edge.example.com. 30 IN A 198.51.100.12
```

Maya (eng-sre): synthetic error rate down to 4.2% now, latency back to baseline. Traces show downstream TLS handshake errors decreased after answers flipped.

Theo (support): Received confirmation from AcmeCorp that errors mostly cleared for them. They saw a short session drop but are green now.

Ava (oncall): Good. Can we identify root cause? Why were Route53 records stale while Cloudflare had the correct set?

Jules (netops): Initial theory: control-plane write lag to Route53 during a previous rollout + DNS cache retention at a subset of resolvers. We saw a partial failure of our config sync job earlier this morning (job id: cfg-sync-881). infra-bot showed a transient S3 throttling error around 1765556400 which likely caused incomplete propagation.

infra-bot: Job cfg-sync-881 FAILED with 503 from s3.amazonaws.com, retry count=2 at 1765556437.

Maya (eng-sre): Correlating timestamps: s3 throttle -> config sync missed TTL change -> Route53 kept old records -> resolvers that queried during window cached old values -> mixed answers across cloudflared/resolvers -> client churn.

Ava (oncall): Action items (short term):
- Jules: leave weights on fallback, monitor 30m
- Maya: run a sweep of synthetic checks across all edge regions, escalate if >1% errors persist
- Theo: update AcmeCorp ticket and notify CS of mitigation and ETA for postmortem
- infra: fix cfg-sync retry backoff and add alert for s3 throttles affecting config sync

Jules (netops): Done with weight flip and lowered TTLs. Will keep fallback live for 35m then reevaluate.

Maya (eng-sre): Running global sweep now. Results: eu-west-1 and eu-west-2 stable. ap-south-1 unaffected. us-west saw no change.

Theo (support): Pinged CS with summary + customer-facing note draft: "We've mitigated an intermittent DNS inconsistency impacting some EU traffic by routing affected domains to a validated fallback pool. We're investigating root cause and will follow up with a post-incident report."

Ava (oncall): Marking P2 -> monitoring. If error rate stays <1% for 30m, we'll transition to postmortem prep.

infra-bot: Scheduled follow-up job: cfg-sync-retry-1765557000 queued (auto backoff jitter enabled).

Maya (eng-sre): Logging note: capture full dig+resolver traces for next 1h for postmortem. I'll attach results to the incident page.

Jules (netops): One more note — Cloudflare showed a TTL respect override for 2 hosts due to a ruleset; that may have caused mismatch. Filing ticket with CF for explanation.

Theo (support): AcmeCorp updated: they appreciate quick fix, asked for timeline for root cause. I told them ~48h for a postmortem.

Ava (oncall): Handing off to morning shift: @Maya will lead postmortem, I'll add notes and timeline. Leaving fallback in place until 09:05 UTC.

Maya (eng-sre): Acknowledged. I'll collect data, diag cfg-sync logs, and correlate with S3 metrics + Cloudflare audit logs.

Ava (oncall): Thanks team. Logging incident as "geo-dns mixed answers -> route53 stale record during cfg-sync throttle" for triage. Will close thread after postmortem link posted. :white_check_mark:

pagerduty-bot: Incident updated: status=monitoring, escalation=resolved -> monitor, alert_rule=geo-dns-resolver-errors.
